body.statement: Within \(\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{SI}}\), Shridharan--Iyengar's canonical reduction for intervention \(a\) has objective \(g\) of degree equal to the number of intervention-touched blocks in \(C\).  Its one-component specialization is linear, its two-component specialization has degree at most two, and for the higher-degree case their Frank--Wolfe method is guaranteed to converge only to an approximate stationary point, rather than to a certified global sharp endpoint.

source.verbatim_statement: The degree of the objective in the new multilinear program is equal to only the number of C-components which are intervened upon in the causal inference problem, instead of the total number of C-components. Our heuristic is guaranteed to converge to a stationary point.

attestation.note: Direct transcription from the primary PMLR PDF, Theorem 4.1 and the Section 5 convergence discussion/Theorem 5.4, retrieved 2026-09-15.
